descriptions.text: Four cases in ten days. $140M gone from Vulcan Forged. "Compromised keys" are so hot right now.

​Chain game project Vulcan Forged officially tweeted that 148 wallets holding PYR were hacked, and more than 4.5 million PYR had been stolen. It then stated: Most of the PYR has been returned from the treasury to the affected wallets.

On December 13, 2021, Vulcan Forged lost approximately $140 million after an attacker compromised its server-side wallet infrastructure, stole private keys for at least 96 user wallets, and drained PYR and other assets. The funds were refunded to affected users, and Vulcan Forged moved to a decentralized wallet system. The semi-custodial wallet system stored user private keys on Vulcan Forged's servers. An attacker gained access to these credentials and exported wallets, resulting in full control over the assets. The model created a single point of failure and violated user-managed key security principles.

Stolen private keys from the blockchain gaming platform Vulcan Forged enabled attackers to siphon funds out of just shy of 100 user wallets. Rather than users managing their own private keys, this is done by the platform, suggesting the issue was not user error. The project says it plans to reimburse users.
